title: Amos: just a herdsman (Amos 7:14–15)
hookLine: "I was no prophet... but I was a herdman", and was sent anyway

lines: WHO DO YOU THINK YOU ARE?
cards: Bethel, the royal sanctuary of the northern kingdom. Amos has been speaking hard words there about the king and the land, and the priest in charge, Amaziah, has had enough.
He sends word to the king that Amos is conspiring. Then he turns to Amos himself: go, flee back to Judah, earn your bread there, prophesy there.
In the King James words: "prophesy not again any more at Bethel: for it is the king's chapel." Who do you think you are?

teach.h: I WAS NO PROPHET, NOR A PROPHET'S SON.
A HERDMAN AND A GATHERER OF FIGS.
teach.b: In the King James words: "I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet's son; but I was an herdman, and a gatherer of sycomore fruit." No credentials. No school.
No family trade. Some readers take a prophet's son to mean a member of a prophetic circle, a trained disciple; either way, Amos says he was not one.
He kept animals and tended sycamore figs, the plain fruit of a working countryside.

teach.h: THE LORD TOOK ME AS I FOLLOWED THE FLOCK.
teach.b: Then the turn: "And the LORD took me as I followed the flock, and the LORD said unto me, Go, prophesy unto my people Israel." Not from a temple, not from a palace.

From behind the animals, in the middle of an ordinary workday. He doesn't argue his qualifications or claim to be more than he is. He says, in effect: I'm not a professional, and I didn't choose this.

teach.h: THE AUTHORITY IS IN THE SENDING.
teach.b: The authority isn't in his résumé. It's in the sending. And there's something quietly bold in it.
Amaziah stands for the official sanctuary, the king's chapel. Amos stands for nothing but the message. His book opens the same way, naming him among the herdmen of Tekoa.
The plain origin isn't hidden; it's the first thing we learn. Whoever kept these words chose to start with the herdsman.

how: Amos is read as one of the Twelve, and passages from his book are read as haftarot in synagogue.

o: the herdsman with no training, taken from the flock and sent
the royal priest who ran the king's chapel at Bethel
a prophet's son, trained from youth in a circle of prophets

games.q: just a herdsman — tap the pairs.
p: what Amos says he never was

s: Amos came from a family of prophets
he says: I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet's son.
the priest at Bethel told Amos to go back to Judah
Amaziah said: prophesy not again any more at Bethel.
Amos defends himself by listing his training
he names his plain work, and says the LORD took him as he followed the flock.

games.q: you're Amos. the king's priest tells you to go home and stop prophesying. what do you say?
o: say you're just a herdsman, and the LORD sent you.
games.why: Amos admits he's no prophet, and says the LORD took him from the flock and said, go.

practice: Think of a place where you've stayed quiet because you weren't the expert, a meeting where something seemed wrong, a family decision, a friend who needed someone to say a hard thing, and let the old reasons rise: I'm not qualified, it's not my place, someone else will.
Hold them, set them down gently, and picture yourself speaking anyway, in your own ordinary words, the way a herdsman would. If you pray, you can ask for the courage to say it.

wordCard.voice: Amos. The herdsman and gatherer of sycamore figs, no prophet and no prophet's son, taken from behind the flock and sent. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: herdsman, the word Amos uses for himself in Amos 7:14.
